headline: Denmark says unauthorised people got CPR data on about 11,000 people in a second breach, stopped by new monitoring.
summary: New incident page. The ministry's Nov 26 press release (s001) gives the second incident: about 11,000 people's CPR numbers, names and addresses reached through irregular lookups from a company, noticed Nov 23, stopped by monitoring added after October; police investigating both cases; security review due before Christmas. DR (s003) and TV 2 (s004) report it from the release; DR adds that the monitoring stopped further leaking. October's 8.8 million incident is recorded as background from the ministry's Oct 5 release (s002) and Help Net Security (s007); the 123456 password report and the company named by Danish media are Reported on IBTimes UK (s008). Main answer Confirmed, filed under hack-stated, on the ministry's own statement. incident_type breach; no service (nothing went down). Size Large. Picture: screenshot of the ministry's notice; the Wikimedia Commons API refused requests (HTTP 429) and its search page showed no photograph of the ministry or the CPR office. Theory sweep: two Hacker News threads on the October breach read (123456 report; CPR numbers not secret), answered as q004 and q005; no thread on the November incident; Reddit blocked. Privacy check done: only the minister, a public official, is named.
author: Research agent
